literal: "Sheng qi xin bu" means the Youhou Empress again sent her trusted follower Shuang Meng to inspect whether the eunuchs she dispatched were trustworthy.
idiomatic: The phrase means the Youhou Empress sent her confidant Shuang Meng to check whether the eunuchs she had dispatched were reliable.

literal: As in Yulan, the sense is that both the dispatched eunuchs and Shuang Meng were men the Youhou Empress trusted.
idiomatic: Yulan’s reading implies that the eunuchs and Shuang Meng alike were people she trusted.

literal: The meanings differ, but both are intelligible.
idiomatic: The senses diverge, yet each construal is defensible.

literal: Now follow the Nan edition and editions below it.
idiomatic: The text follows Nan and the editions descended from it.

literal: Then bestowed on the empress a farewell testament. Beishi juan 13 and Yulan
idiomatic: She was then given a parting testament. Beishi juan 13 and Yulan

literal: Zhang Senkai held the character "si" to be superfluous.
idiomatic: Zhang Senkai regarded "si" as an interpolation.

literal: Comment: "Sijue" (death testament) means swearing never to meet again—it is also intelligible; retained as is.
idiomatic: Note: "Death testament" can mean a vow never to meet again—that sense works too, so the wording is kept.

literal: Then acted as proxy in performing the initial sacrifice. Yulan juan 140
idiomatic: She then officiated by proxy at the first sacrifice. Yulan juan 140
The graph for "initial" (chu) is given as "sacrifice" (ci) in that witness.

literal: Comment: Above it says "The Empress Dowager, because Suzong was young and not yet able to sacrifice in person," etc.—then it was not only the initial sacrifice.
idiomatic: Note: The passage above says Suzong was too young to sacrifice in person, so she did more than merely the first rite.
